e: The IDF announces that an Israeli civilian entered Lebanon illegally near the Rosh HaNikra Crossing, adding that UN peacekeepers discovered him close to the border and handed him over to its soldiers for return to Israel.
President Herzog formally gives MK Eisenkot the mandate and assigns him the responsibility of establishing a new government.
Ra'am declares that even in the absence of a formal coalition agreement, it would vote to back a government headed by Eisenkot.

The Joint List announces that it will support Gadi Eisenkot as Prime Minister, providing him the majority of recommendations, adding that it will support the minority government externally and that it will not topple it in the event of a security emergency.
Israel and Germany extend their energy partnership into 2027.

Clalit Health Services and Schneider Children's Medical Center announce the launch of Schneider Children's Venture Capital, Israel's first venture capital investment fund dedicated to pediatric healthcare innovation and the third fund of its kind globally.
US President Donald Trump announces that the US will terminate all military aid to Israel, totaling $4 billion per year, by the end of 2026, but will continue to sell military hardware.
A 3,300-year-old Egyptian amulet dating to the Late Bronze Age is discovered by a 17-year-old American boy from Tel Gezer National Park in the Judaean Foothills.
The IDF withdraws from several Hebron neighborhoods after an 11-day raid.
Elbit Systems and the Defense Ministry sign a $190 million contract for a new artillery training facility.
Intel agrees to acquire Israeli startup Classiq Technologies, in a deal estimated to be worth more than $2 billion.
Israel agrees to provide an offshore patrol vessel to Cyprus.
Artem Dolgopyat finishes in third place in the floor exercise at the Artistic Gymnastics World Championships in Netherlands.

Two IDF soldiers are killed and three other soldiers are wounded in a gun attack at the Judea Junction on Route 35. The two attackers are shot dead by the IDF at the scene. In response, Prime Minister Netanyahu orders a "full lockdown" of the West Bank.
The Hebrew University of Jerusalem declares that it will rename its Mount Scopus campus for John Paulson following a record $250M donation.
Dov Lior, a hardline Orthodox rabbi, issues a halachic ruling permitting Jews to take Palestinian olives, framing it as a fulfillment of the conquering of the Land of Israel.
Justice Yael Willner is appointed by the High Court to the Judicial Selection Committee.
Colombia inaugurates its embassy in Jerusalem.

Former Shin Bet director Ronen Bar files a NIS 3 million (approximately $975,000) defamation suit against Prime Minister Netanyahu, citing warnings issued prior to the 7 October attacks, for alleging that Bar was aware of the threat of a Hamas attack in the hours leading up to October 7, 2023, but chose not to inform Netanyahu.
Israel agrees to purchase 12 Boeing Apache helicopters.
A Bedouin man who joined the IDF to spy for the Mujahideen Brigades is sentenced to 24.5 years imprisonment.
Defense Minister Israel Katz declares a nationwide six-month ban on fiber optic drones.
Israel returns 22 artifacts recovered from the illegal antiquities trade to Greece.
The Supreme Court directs the government and the IDF to disclose a timeframe for the return of Palestinians displaced in the northern section of the West Bank.
A Hezbollah unexploded munition detonation in the Ramim Ridge region kills one child and injures 24 others, including schoolchildren and teachers.
Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar and Albanian Foreign Minister Ferit Hoxha sign an enlarged government-to-government cooperation agreement.

The Yesha Council announces that Defense Minister Israel Katz has ordered a ban on pro-Palestinian activists, whether Israeli or foreign, seeking to assist Palestinian olive growers in the West Bank during the harvest season, citing the Council's demand to prevent activists from "coming to the olive harvest area to create provocations and confrontations."
Israel participates in the Marrakech Airshow in Morocco for the first time since the Abraham Accords.
Following the IDF's recommendation, Defense Minister Israel Katz announces that crossings into the West Bank and Gaza will be closed during the days marking the 7 October attacks.

After the Flydubai Flight 1073 incident, the Israeli government admits that it does not independently vet foreign pilots. Prime Minister Netanyahu orders "a through review" of security procedures for international flights to Israel.
One person is killed and another individual is wounded after a small aircraft crashes along Route 65, in the vicinity of Kafr Qara.
The Supreme Court overturns the Central Elections Committee's ban on Arab parties running for the 2026 Israeli legislative election.
A group of Israelis are rescued from Lalibela following days of being stuck due to fighting in Tigray.
Prime Minister Netanyahu announces new security measures in response to the Flydubai Flight 1073.
An Israeli airstrike kills Izz al-Din al-Beik, head of Al-Qassam Brigades in northern Gaza.

Likud announces that Prime Minister Netanyahu has sued media outlets Haaretz, Yedioth Ahronoth, Channel 12, and journalists Shlomi Eldar, Uri Misgav, Nadav Eyal, Barak Ravid, and Attila Somfalvi, among others, for NIS 2.6 million ($850,000) over recent reports that he received warnings from UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed and Egypt's intelligence chief Abbas Kamel before the 7 October attacks.
The IDF announces that it prevented an attempt to transfer munitions from Jordan to Israel with a drone.
Defense Minister Israel Katz announces a "general closure" on the West Bank following a recommendation from the IDF, preventing Palestinian laborers from entering settlements amidst Sukkot.
Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announces that Israel will revoke diplomatic privileges and Israel-issued credentials of Dutch diplomats in Ramallah due to a settlement trade ban.

Prime Minister Netanyahu orders the drafting of an ICC case against Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, citing Turkey's alleged persecution of Kurdish minorities and the Turkish government's alleged financial assistance for Hamas.
